title: Told in New York he needs a second spinal operation
summary: In 1947, with three months of bookings and cars bought, a doctor tells Cobb the operation must be repeated; he drives bitterly to dinner at Joe Thomas's home.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: I'll tell you how it happened. I'm at 124th and Madison Avenue in a hospital for [joint]disease, for my second spinal operation, which made me bitter. I had 3 months of bookings, but let me back up a minute.
When I first went in they told me after the operation by that doctor, "You will have 4 months of bed rest and 2 months of convalescence and then you can go on back, you know. And I went by that.

And I went up to Greenwood Lake, up in the section of the woods that Sugar Ray Robinson was training, up in the mountains, I carried and I had my wife up there; I bought 2 cars, with promissory notes from my agent; getting ready to go on the road with 3 months of bookings, and come back, but I still didn't feel right.

I went in to rehearsal one day, go back for my final examination, the next day, early, to go back for a second day of rehearsals, have given the itinerary out, and this man slapped me in my face and said, "You've got to have this operation over again."

I couldn't believe it. This was the first time my wife never went with me. I drove from downtown, uptown, and I don't know if I ran a red light or what, because I was just crazy as hell, and luckily, I made it. I was going to Joe Thomas and Laverne's house -- they lived right around the corner from me at 160th St. Nicholas for dinner, and I didn't tell my wife nothing.
And Laverne and Joe said, "What's wrong with you?" and I said, "Oh, I'm all right." I didn't say nothing to my wife yet. I am so bitter and so disgusted.
So you say you hadn't said anything to your wife yet?

I said I hadn't said anything to my wife yet, and I was at Joe Thomas and Laverne Thomas's house at 160th, who lived around the corner, and I had gone there for dinner, and found I had to loosen up, because they kept asking me what's wrong with me. Well, naturally I can't be too lively, knowing that the man said I had to have the operation over again, is what I'm saying to you.
